comment: Deepen angle catalog. Each entry: slug + name + category + description (1-2 lines, fed to selector) + tags (selector matches against selection content) + needs (must-run-before this angle, e.g. occam needs leo+lung). timeoutMs is per-stage cap. The selector picks 5-6 of these per Cmd+D invocation; synth always runs last and is NOT in this catalog.

angles.name: first-principles atom strip
angles.description: Decomposes claim into base atoms; rejects analogy; tests necessity boundaries. Pick when the user's selection makes a strong claim that should be verified from primitives.

angles.name: Bayesian belief update
angles.description: Prior P(claim) → evidence likelihood ratio → posterior. Pick when there is a probabilistic claim, a decision under uncertainty, or evidence-weighing language.

angles.name: razor / pruning
angles.description: Cuts redundant or weaker claims; keeps the load-bearing core. Pick when other angles produce many candidates that need triage.

angles.name: internal contradiction surfacing
angles.description: Finds inconsistencies between selection and its own implications, or between claim and its method. Pick when the selection is dense + assertive + likely to have hidden tensions.

angles.name: Toyota five-whys cascade
angles.description: Drills from symptom to fundamental cause via 4-5 sequential 'why' steps. Pick when selection describes an outcome, problem, or behavior, and asks 'why is X happening'.

angles.name: counterfactual variation
angles.description: Changes one variable in the selection's setup; describes the resulting world; what the difference reveals about the original. Pick when selection has dependencies that benefit from variation testing.

angles.name: 2nd / 3rd order consequences
angles.description: Extends the chain past the stated 1st-order outcome. What happens to other actors / systems / incentives 2-3 hops out? Pick when the selection proposes an action, decision, or architectural choice.

angles.name: testable prediction extraction
angles.description: Extracts what observation would confirm or falsify the selection's claim. What data exists; what experiment would test. Pick when selection has empirical claim or hypothesis-shaped statement.

angles.name: divergent cross-domain analogy
angles.description: 5+ frames from unrelated fields (sport, biology, music, surgery, jazz, etc). Pick when selection's content is stuck in one domain or wants a 'fresh angle'.

angles.name: structural match across domains
angles.description: Predicate-graph match: this domain X mirrors that domain Y. Different from analogy — about deep structural identity, not surface similarity. Pick when selection has a process or system structure.

angles.name: historical case anchor
angles.description: 'This happened before in [domain] in [year], outcome was Z'. Pick when selection makes a forward-looking claim that has historical analogues, OR when grounding in a real case helps.

angles.name: adversarial attack
angles.description: 3 concrete counterexamples on the strongest claim. Doesn't hedge; doesn't say 'on the other hand'. Pick when selection has an assertion that benefits from being stress-tested.

angles.name: steelman the opposite
angles.description: Builds the strongest version of the directly opposite position. Pick when the selection takes a strong stance and a strong counter-stance would test it.

angles.name: QAQ inversion / pre-mortem
angles.description: Pretends the plan failed; works backward from failure to identify causes. Pick when selection describes a plan, design, or system likely to be fielded.

angles.name: weakest assumption identification
angles.description: Finds the SINGLE weakest load-bearing assumption — if it breaks, everything else falls. Pick when selection has multiple chained claims.

angles.name: Feynman compression
angles.description: Explain to a smart 12-year-old in ≤5 paragraphs. No jargon. The compression itself reveals the unclear. Pick when selection is dense, technical, or seeks lossy crystallization.

angles.name: incompatible framings
angles.description: Re-presents the same content in 3 incompatible framings (e.g. economic / aesthetic / political; engineering / ritual / social). Pick when selection benefits from multi-perspectival reframing.

angles.name: YC partner — single move
angles.description: What's the SINGLE move that, if done now, makes the curve nonlinear over 12 months? Identifies the highest-leverage decision. Pick when selection is about a project, choice, or strategy.

angles.name: frontier web research
angles.description: Real web search for relevant 2024-2026 sources; provenance with URLs. DATE-CONSTRAINED — never cites future years. Pick when selection makes empirical or technical claim that benefits from external grounding.
